title: AlphaFold modeling guides discovery of RPA as a human telomerase processivity factor
summary: RPA was identified as a telomerase processivity factor that stimulates telomerase in vitro. AlphaFold modeling predicted that RPA engages a telomerase surface distinct from the one bound by TPP1; guided by this, engineered TERT separation-of-function mutants lost RPA-mediated stimulation and showed impaired telomere elongation, and short-telomere disease-associated TERT mutations reduced RPA-dependent stimulation. AlphaFold served as a guide within extensive wet-lab experiments.
ai_technology: AlphaFold structural modeling predicting the RPA-telomerase interface

evidence.tested: In vitro telomerase assays and cell telomere-length experiments with engineered mutants.
evidence.unknown: The AlphaFold-predicted interface is described as a prediction in the abstract; its direct structural confirmation is not stated; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: AlphaFold modeling predicted the interface that guided design of separation-of-function mutants.
